assessment: Explicit managed-runtime source review on 2026-11-22 of the default server's DTLS execution path at commit a8e9ce1468c8741b4f2b9b17f8c1fd5d68eb24e6, src tree 03afba95d5e9f8e144cce7425a6d0b7fbc9a4678. The three vendored mediasoup trees and vendor/native-components.json are byte-identical to the previously reviewed bindings: mediasoup 0.29.0 still creates an in-process Rust thread that calls mediasoup_worker_run, the worker still checks SSL_CTX_set_max_proto_version(..., DTLS1_2_VERSION) after creating its context, and the authenticated-close, fingerprint, SRTP and owned X509-name patches remain present. DTLS uses the authenticated static OpenSSL 4.1.0 with shared, dso, module and engine loading disabled; AWS-LC 5.11.0 stays the authenticated static crypto archive. The first-party src delta from the previously reviewed tree 10f6d70a7d356fc85eb0cb0aac910adec5cb625c (121 changed paths) was inventoried for production process execution, dynamic-library or module loading, iconv/gconv locale conversion, filesystem access, outbound network destinations, environment reads and cryptographic calls, with inline and separate cfg(test) modules set apart. It adds no process execution, dynamic loading, locale conversion or outbound destination, and environment reads stay in src/config.rs. Filesystem access shrinks: migrations are embedded at build time instead of being read from ./migrations, and the server only checks at startup that web/dist/index.html exists before serving the unchanged web/dist static route. jsonwebtoken is removed: attachment grants are HMAC-SHA256 and Web Push VAPID tokens ES256, both signed through aws-lc-rs on the same static AWS-LC; access tokens draw from the operating system's random source; sha2 computes short public digests. The new operator subcommand issue-account-recovery uses the existing database pool and standard output only, and is not the fixed managed server command. Web Push keeps its approved provider hosts, disabled redirects and proxy discovery, deadlines and concurrency. The default server's x86_64 Linux normal-dependency graph differs from the reviewed one only by dropping jsonwebtoken, signature and zeroize_derive and by async-executor 1.14.0 to 1.14.1, rustix 1.1.5 to 1.1.6, form_urlencoded 1.2.2 to 1.2.3 and url 2.5.8 to 2.5.9, the release that fixes RUSTSEC-2026-0592; sqlx gains only its build-time macros feature, and the new workspace members are tooling crates outside that graph. The vendor/integrity.json change records only the vendored tasks.py message of the fuzzer-run-all developer task. The image tier performs the runtime checks in Rust: the ELF audit (crates/security/src/elf.rs) refuses loader hooks, RPATH/RUNPATH and differing standard-directory candidates; the runtime proof (crates/security/src/image/runtime.rs) requires the native record's static OpenSSL 4.1.0 and disabled options, the image defaults that simplestchat-ops release profile requires, no loader cache, preload list or hwcaps directory, and the exact security/runtime/nsswitch.conf. ops/ansible/files/runtime_profile.py stays bound because the proof requires it and the host release helpers still validate compose and environment settings with it; its bytes and the NSS configuration are unchanged. This assessment covers the intended production execution path, not every unused dependency API, engine-provided init, administrator-selected program or post-deployment mutation, and it certifies no release image: archive and final-binary identity, runtime restrictions and image vulnerability disposition remain independently enforced, and changed source or profile bytes require a fresh review. The review spans the 60 days a source review may cover.
